name: PixaFilm
title: PixaFilm User Manual
scope: Product workflows, account access, recovery and updates. Source-backed tool tours are included where a registered tool catalog is connected; this is not a complete reference for every editor command.

chapters.title: Start a first project
chapters.body: Import a few short clips and place them in a sequence. Work with copies of important footage. Help → PixaFilm User Manual (also F1) opens this offline guide. Help → Quick Tool Tour explains all 17 timeline tools with Next, Back, Finish and Escape; visible tool groups are highlighted without changing your active tool or project.

chapters.title: Make a first edit
chapters.body: Arrange clips on the timeline, trim their beginnings and ends, and preview the cuts. Listen to the audio as well as watching the image.

chapters.title: Keep your work organized
chapters.body: Keep original media available at its original path. Use clearly named tracks and sequences so the project remains understandable.

chapters.title: Save and export
chapters.body: Save the project separately from the rendered video. Preview the exported result from beginning to end before sharing it. If the device access refresh fails, keep the app open and use Save recovery copy to choose a destination. Reconnect before closing if you have unfinished text fields or background operations. Open the recovered native files in the editor after reconnecting; retain the original files.

chapters.title: Your account
chapters.body: Use Your account in the Pixa footer to connect this device. Pixa is free early access with no card requirement and no scheduled account expiration. Only approve the code displayed on your own device. Device access refreshes online; a disconnected, revoked or signed-out device must reconnect. Your files remain local.

chapters.title: Updates
chapters.body: Use Updates in the Pixa footer to check the Pixa publisher feed. On Mac, download the candidate, save your work and choose Install and restart. The app checks the installer digest, Apple publisher signature, bundle identity and Gatekeeper before replacement. A canceled editor-close prompt cancels the pending restart. Windows and Linux open the Pixa download page. No update is offered until a matching publisher release exists. PixaFilm checks its own publisher feed in the background once at startup. A matching available update opens the Updates window. Downloading and installation still require your choice.

chapters.title: Find your way around
chapters.body: The menu bar and editor panels contain the main controls. Use the existing workspace controls to show a hidden panel. Manual and Quick tour in the Pixa footer reopen this help without changing the project.

chapters.title: Undo and safe experiments
chapters.body: Use Undo to reverse a normal document edit, and Redo to restore it. Keep an original project or duplicate before destructive operations. Undo does not reverse an external file deletion, a published upload or every background operation.

chapters.title: Linked files and portability
chapters.body: An editable project may refer to media, fonts, textures or other external files. Keep those resources alongside your project in a stable folder. Copy the complete folder when moving computers and reopen it before removing the original.

chapters.title: Working with another application
chapters.body: Save a native editable copy before exporting an interchange format. Features such as effects, fonts and linked resources may differ in another application. Reopen exported files in the destination application before relying on them.

chapters.title: Recovery and backups
chapters.body: Save regularly and keep a separate backup of important projects and original media. Recovery copies contain committed project state; unfinished text fields, external files and background tasks may need separate attention. Restore into a new project or folder rather than overwriting the original.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
chapters.body: For missing content, check the active document, selected object, visible panels, layers and linked-file paths. For account problems, reconnect in Your account. For failed updates, keep the existing application and use the verified Pixa download page; do not disable operating-system security checks.

tools.title: Selection Tool
tools.body: Select, move and trim clips in the timeline. Drag a clip body to move it or an edge to adjust a cut.

tools.title: Track Select Forward Tool
tools.body: Select clips from the clicked position forward so a group of later edits can move together.

tools.title: Track Select Backward Tool
tools.body: Select clips before the clicked position for a coordinated timeline move.

tools.title: Ripple Edit Tool
tools.body: Trim a clip while closing or opening the adjacent timeline gap; later clips can shift.

tools.title: Rolling Edit Tool
tools.body: Move a cut between neighboring clips while keeping their combined duration unchanged.

tools.title: Rate Stretch Tool
tools.body: Change a clip's timeline duration by changing playback speed. Check the resulting motion and audio.

tools.title: Remix Tool
tools.body: Adjust music to fit a target duration. Listen to the transitions before exporting.

tools.title: Razor Tool
tools.body: Cut a clip at the clicked timeline position. Select the pieces afterward to move or remove them.

tools.title: Slip Tool
tools.body: Change which source frames appear inside a clip without moving its timeline boundaries.

tools.title: Slide Tool
tools.body: Move a clip while trimming its neighboring clips to preserve the surrounding sequence length.

tools.title: Pen Tool
tools.body: Add or adjust clip keyframes to change properties over time.

tools.title: Rectangle Tool
tools.body: Draw a rectangular graphic or mask in the viewer.

tools.title: Ellipse Tool
tools.body: Draw an elliptical graphic or mask in the viewer.

tools.title: Hand Tool
tools.body: Pan the timeline or viewer without moving project content.

tools.title: Zoom Tool
tools.body: Change the timeline or viewer magnification; this does not change export resolution.

tools.title: Type Tool
tools.body: Create or edit horizontal text for titles and graphics.

tools.title: Vertical Type Tool
tools.body: Create or edit text arranged vertically.
